name: Reinforcement Learning
strandNote: Optional for every role. Useful for research on execution, market making and other decisions made in sequence.
description: Learn to act from rewards: bandits, Bellman equations, Q-learning, policy gradients and game-tree search.

skills.rl-mdp: Markov decision processes and dynamic programming

requires.why: Thompson sampling updates a belief about each arm with Bayes' rule after every pull.
The UCB bonus comes from a tail bound, built up from Chebyshev's inequality.
Thompson sampling draws win rates from Beta posteriors, the Beta family taught there.
Uses standard errors of a win rate and the Beta-prior update of a coin.
A policy's value solves the same first-step equations as an expected time to absorption.
Value iteration is the dice game's backward induction run with no last roll.
A baseline is a control variate: it cuts the gradient estimate's variance without bias.
Trains a softmax policy network with the array autograd built there.

lessonNames.l10-one-step-ahead: Learning one step at a time
lessonNames.l12-safe-or-greedy: The safe path and the greedy path
lessonNames.l15-baselines: A baseline is a control variate

lessonObjectives.l1-which-machine: Write a bandit simulator and measure regret against always playing the best arm.
lessonObjectives.l2-exploring-at-random: Build an epsilon-greedy agent with running means, and explain the regret it cannot avoid.
lessonObjectives.l3-optimism: Derive the UCB bonus from a tail bound and code the UCB1 agent.
lessonObjectives.l4-sampling-beliefs: Build a Thompson sampling agent from Beta posteriors and compare three agents' regret.
lessonObjectives.l5-states-and-rewards: Model a problem as a Markov decision process and write the discounted return.
lessonObjectives.l6-what-a-policy-is-worth: Derive a fixed policy's Bellman equation and solve it as a linear system.
lessonObjectives.l7-value-iteration: Code value iteration and bound its error by the discount factor.
lessonObjectives.l8-improving-a-policy: Build policy iteration and check that it reaches value iteration's policy.
lessonObjectives.l9-learning-from-episodes: Write Monte Carlo policy evaluation from sampled episodes.
lessonObjectives.l10-one-step-ahead: Code TD(0) and compare its error with Monte Carlo on a random walk.
lessonObjectives.l11-q-learning: Build a Q-learning agent whose greedy policy matches value iteration on a gridworld.
lessonObjectives.l12-safe-or-greedy: Compare SARSA and Q-learning on a cliff, and explain on-policy against off-policy learning.
lessonObjectives.l13-a-policy-with-dials: Write a softmax policy and find where a stochastic policy beats every deterministic one.
lessonObjectives.l14-reinforce: Derive the score-function gradient and code REINFORCE.
lessonObjectives.l15-baselines: Derive why a baseline leaves the gradient unbiased, and measure the variance it removes.
lessonObjectives.l16-a-policy-network: Build a policy network with the array autograd and train it with REINFORCE and a baseline.
lessonObjectives.l17-minimax: Code minimax and find the value of a small game.
lessonObjectives.l18-pruning-the-tree: Implement alpha-beta pruning and a table of seen positions, and count the work saved.
lessonObjectives.l19-tree-search: Build Monte Carlo tree search with the UCB rule in the tree.
lessonObjectives.l20-self-play: Train a value table by self-play and explain how AlphaZero extends the idea.
